title: Denser rewards without reward hacking: potential-based shaping, paid once
purpose: A fixed reward for running the tests pays an agent that runs them forever. Potential-based shaping pays only for new progress on the environment's real state. Compare both on a scripted looping agent, on a scripted agent that patches the test framework, and on every real trajectory, against the verified outcome.

checks.description: the looping agent earns a growing fixed reward and nothing from potential-based shaping
checks.because: Its actions never change the state, so Phi never rises; the fixed reward pays every repeat.

checks.description: the framework-patching agent gets no progress, because Phi is measured in a fresh copy
checks.because: In place its patch makes every example 'pass' (Phi in place 1.0); the fresh copy restores nothing it may not change, and the tamper check zeroes Phi.

checks.description: potential-based shaping tracks success better than a reward for running tests
checks.because: Phi rises exactly when an issue example starts to give the expected value; running tests says nothing about whether anything was fixed.
